parts.text:
But it gets more complicated once fragrance hits the skin.

How skin chemistry enters the picture

While a paper

strip is a fairly neutral surface, we have various molecules on the skin. These interact with the perfume and can not only change the order of the molecules being released, but also alter or mask the resulting

.

The main skin factors that will influence the scent of perfume are:

moisture content and oiliness

temperature

pH level

microbiome.

Moisture and oiliness

Hydration is one of the main factors. Dry skin tends to

heavier or larger fragrance molecules more readily, while moist or oily skin provides a better surface for fragrance molecules to sit on and evaporate gradually.

This often improves how long the perfume lasts and its projection – how much others around you can

it. This is why the same perfume could last all day on one person, but only for a couple of hours on another.

Temperature

Warmer skin increases evaporation, causing perfumes to develop more quickly and sometimes smell stronger. A person with
warmer skin may experience top notes disappearing much faster. Base notes may become noticeable within minutes rather than an hour. This can make it seem as though the perfume “

” the top notes.

pH level

The natural acidity of the skin, often referred to as skin pH, may also subtly influence fragrance performance. Human skin is slightly acidic, typically around pH 4.5 to 5.5.

While most fragrance ingredients remain

within this range, subtle pH changes could cause fragrance ingredients to react differently. As a result some floral notes may weaken, some musks may become more prominent, some citrus notes may smell sharper or disappear

.

Skin microbiome

Perhaps the most fascinating factor is our skin microbiome. Our skin is home to billions of microorganisms, including bacteria and fungi. These microbes interact with compounds found in

and skin oils, producing volatile organic compounds that contribute to each person’s unique scent profile.

The microbes can also metabolise fragrance molecules. This can produce new odours, enhance some notes, or

others. It’s another reason why a fragrance could smell wonderful on one person and unpleasant on another.

Perfumes can be fickle

questions.prompt: Which statement best summarises the overall focus of this article?
options: A compass works by aligning a magnetised needle with Earth's magnetic field.
An unusual pair of stars helps explain a repeating radio signal from a dead star.
Individual skin conditions change how perfume molecules evaporate and how a fragrance smells.
